units.name: Jarmen Kell

tier.basis: Trained at the GLA Barracks once a Palace stands: his 1.04 Object file lists both buildings as prerequisites and the wiki infobox names the Palace. The Palace is the GLA's single tech building, which the tier map puts at t3, and the base-game manual tags him as a unit that building unlocks. The Toxin, Demolition and Stealth Generals all field him behind their own Barracks and Palace, so no GLA general lacks him. Each player may have only one Kell alive at a time (MaxSimultaneousOfType in the Object file; the Zero Hour Academy tip says the same of all three heroes), and a new one can be trained once he dies. A player who has captured another GLA general's buildings can also train that general's Kell (wiki).

cost_band.basis: His list price, the same for every GLA general's version, lands exactly on the very-high threshold and so takes that band; it is about twice the anchor price of the three basic battle tanks.

mobility.notes: His land speed is half again a Ranger's (the wiki infobox; his own locomotor in the 1.04 files agrees), exactly on the medium edge, which the band rules send to medium; the wiki calls him quick for a foot soldier. Like most units he slows down when badly hurt, which the band leaves out. His locomotor has no cliff surface, so no climb trait; a Combat Cycle carries him over ground he could not cross on foot (wiki).

armour.notes: Step 1 of the armour-class steps decided: his armour set is Human Armor (1.04 Object file; the wiki infobox lists its values), the set the Ranger, Pathfinder and Rebel also wear, which the armour_map makes unarmoured; the soldier rule keeps him there, since his set is no tougher than the basic rifleman's. He has only a little more health than a Ranger. The set takes double damage from sniper fire and from being crushed, half again from flame and particle beams, half from lasers and only a tenth from tank shells and infantry missiles. Only the Overlord and the Emperor can run him over (see strengths). The self-healing of Elite and Heroic ranks belongs to veterancy and is left off.

sensors.notes: His fog-clearing figure equals the Ranger's, so the band is medium; his targeting figure, half his fog-clearing one, is twice the Ranger's, which is what the wiki means when it praises his sight. He could detect stealthed units until Zero Hour patch 1.03 took that away (wiki changelog), and his 1.04 Object file gives him no detector, so no sensor trait. His own stealth is coded as the cloak passive (abilities/1), as the registry's Generals stealth note asks, not as the stealth sensor trait.

armament.name: Sniper rifle
armament.summary: A scoped rifle that fires one slow, deliberate shot at a time; the game data has each shot land the instant it is fired. It reaches a little over twice as far as the Ranger's rifle, well inside his own fog-clearing sight. Its sniper damage counts double against the armour every ordinary soldier wears, so each hit is enough to drop a basic rifleman. Vehicles, aircraft and nearly all buildings take nothing from it, which also stops him aiming at them: the Fire Base, which takes sniper fire in full, is the one building it hurts, and he can shoot the soldiers who crew a Stinger Site. Soldiers garrisoned in a building are out of its reach. AP Bullets, bought once at the Black Market for several GLA units, makes it hit a quarter harder.

crew.notes: One player is Kell. He takes one seat in a transport and garrisons buildings like other infantry (game-wide), and he can ride a Combat Cycle, which then fires his rifle and his snipe and hides as he does (see combos). In Zero Hour, if he climbs into an emptied vehicle himself, another Kell can be trained (wiki).

abilities.name: Sniper Attack
abilities.summary: His one button besides the basic orders. He fires a special round at one enemy vehicle within his rifle's reach: the hull is not harmed, but its crew dies, and the vehicle halts, turns neutral and stands empty until a soldier climbs in. Any infantry unit can then claim it for its owner (a game-wide rule), so his own troops can drive it away, or the enemy can win it back. Every crewed ground vehicle is a valid target, from trucks up to the Overlord, however thick its armour. Riders of a sniped transport are pushed out within reach of his rifle, a sniped car bomb explodes, and a Combat Cycle is lost either way: blown up if it is moving, or scuttled once its rider is shot if it stands still. A construction dozer emptied this way and then claimed lets the GLA build the enemy's structures. Uncrewed machines such as the Sentry Drone take nothing from it, nor do aircraft or buildings. The shot gives him away, cannot be fired from inside a building, and then takes about half a minute to be ready again.

abilities.name: Camouflage
abilities.summary: He is invisible to the enemy at all times except while attacking: each rifle shot or snipe shows him, and a couple of seconds after he stops he vanishes again. An enemy detector nearby, such as a Pathfinder, a Sentry Drone or a Listening Outpost, uncovers him, and the moment he is uncovered the game sends idle enemy units in range after him. The same stealth lets him slip into a civilian building and shoot from it without the enemy noticing that it is occupied. Coded as one passive with the cloak pattern, as the registry's Generals stealth note asks.

on_death.notes: In the sources he is simply gone: his Object file has death animations and no blast, so the infantry default applies. Since only one may live at a time, a new Kell can be trained once he is dead. The Demolition General's version, recorded under this entry, differs in two ways that are not coded here: even without upgrades it can plant timed and remote demolition charges on enemy buildings, buttons the other versions lack (wiki), and that general's side-wide Demolitions upgrade, bought at his Palace, adds a button to blow himself up and makes him explode when he dies.

strengths.why: His rifle drops an ordinary soldier with each hit from a little over twice a rifleman's reach, and his build tooltip names infantry as what he is strong against.
Sniper Attack kills the crew of any crewed ground vehicle, Overlord included, whatever its armour, and leaves the hull for the GLA to take; the tooltip names vehicles as his other strength.
He stays invisible until he fires, and he can sit in a civilian building and shoot from it while the enemy thinks it empty (manual, tooltip).
As a hero he cannot be flattened by ordinary vehicles: only the Overlord and the Emperor can run him over.

weaknesses.why: His rifle cannot touch vehicles, aircraft, nearly any building or soldiers inside a garrison, so between snipes he has no answer to armour and none at all to fliers.
The snipe takes about half a minute to recharge, so a group of vehicles overwhelms him and the enemy has time to take an emptied hull back; he also cannot snipe from inside a building.
Once he is seen he is as frail as any foot soldier: his armour set takes double damage from enemy snipers and extra from flame.
Only one Kell per player at a time, at a very high price and behind the Palace.

countered_by.why: Official text, his build tooltip, lists scouts as the one thing he is weak against.

Detection strips his only defence: the wiki names Pathfinders and armed Sentry Drones, which see through stealth and cut down infantry, and a campaign hint sends Listening Outposts to stop him sniping vehicles.
Machines without a crew shrug off his snipe; the wiki singles out the Sentry Drone, which also detects him, outruns him and can still hit him while he rides a Combat Cycle.
The same reason: the wiki calls the unmanned, stealth-detecting Sentry Drone one of the gravest threats to him.
Nothing he carries can attack a flier, and the wiki notes that he has no defence against aircraft.

Enemy snipers hurt him badly, since his armour set takes double damage from sniper fire, and the Pathfinder's rifle outreaches his; the wiki counts a Combat Cycle as cover from counter-sniping Pathfinders and enemy Kells.

counters.why: Each rifle hit kills a basic soldier from well outside a rifleman's reach, and he hides again between shots; the tooltip names infantry first among his strengths.
Sniper Attack takes any crewed ground vehicle out of the fight in one shot, from a truck to an Overlord, and leaves it for his side to capture; the tooltip names vehicles as his other strength.
Sniping a transport's crew throws its riders out into the open, where his rifle picks them off (wiki).

An enemy GLA player's Stinger Sites, anti-air defences manned by soldiers, lose those soldiers to his rifle, leaving the site open for the rest of the army to destroy (wiki); the Fire Base is the one building that takes his sniper fire in full.

combos.why: Any soldier can climb into a vehicle he has emptied, so infantry close by turn each snipe into a stolen vehicle; the manual and a campaign hint both pair him with GLA infantry for this.
Riding a Combat Cycle, he keeps his rifle, his snipe and his stealth on a quicker mount that crosses rough ground, out of reach of counter-snipers (hint and wiki).
The same reason: the Combat Cycle is the bike whose weapon he sets when he rides it.
He has no defence against aircraft, so the wiki advises keeping anti-air at hand wherever the enemy rules the sky.

units.memorable: A camouflaged mercenary sniper who shoots the crew out of any enemy ground vehicle, Overlord included, and leaves the empty hull for his own infantry to drive away.
units.as_player: The team's one hero pick at T3, a hidden marksman. Left mouse fires a slow sniper rifle that drops a soldier per hit from beyond rifle range but cannot hurt vehicles, aircraft or almost any building. Q (Sniper Attack) shoots the crew out of an enemy vehicle, leaving the hull neutral for any teammate on foot to take; it then recharges for about half a minute. You stay invisible until you shoot, but detectors give you away, and nothing you carry touches aircraft.

sources.title: Command & Conquer: Generals manual (UK, PC), scan hosted by the Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: EA's printed manual; the Command & Conquer Wiki hosts the scan. Kell's row in the GLA unit table, printed page 40: Purpose Scout and Base Infiltration, the Structure Upgrade tag, and a description of a stealthy sniper who can hold a building unseen and shoot the drivers out of vehicles so that GLA infantry can take them. Read in a layout text dump of the PDF; paraphrases checked by hand, since the copy-check cannot read it.

sources.title: Jarmen Kell, Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Read through the MediaWiki API, from the page cache's copy (fetched 2026-10-19). Infobox: price, Barracks and Palace, health, the Human armour set with its values, land speed, both sight figures, rifle reach, the Sniper damage of the rifle and the Kill Pilot damage of the snipe, both reload figures, the Demolition General's charges and the AP Bullets upgrade. Prose: what the snipe does, his stealth and hidden garrisoning, his counters (Pathfinders, Sentry Drones, aircraft, detection) and tactics (infantry to claim vehicles, the Combat Cycle, anti-air). Changelog: detection removed in Zero Hour patch 1.03. Its Strong vs. and Weak vs. bullets match the 1.04 tooltip but are the wiki's own words.

sources.title: generals.str, plain-text copy of the Zero Hour 1.04 string table, TheSuperHackers' GeneralsGamePatch repository on GitHub
sources.version: Zero Hour 1.04 (the file's first version, which matches the binary original)
sources.note: Copies the in-game text, as the registry note says; read from the page cache's copy (fetched 2026-10-20). Every Kell build button in the unedited 1.04 CommandButton.ini of the same repository (main GLA, Toxin, Demolition and Stealth Generals) points to CONTROLBAR:ToolTipGLABuildJarmenKell: he is camouflaged, can hide in civilian buildings to snipe soldiers and kills vehicle crews so that the vehicles can be captured; its last two lines name infantry and vehicles as his strengths and scouts as his weakness. His Sniper Attack button (CONTROLBAR:SniperAttack) has the tooltip ToolTipGLAFireJarmenKellVehicleSnipe, which says it kills a vehicle's crew. Hints and tips: HELP:CombatCycle-04 (he keeps sniping while riding a Combat Cycle), MDGLA03:Help-JarmenKell-01 (the snipe lets infantry capture enemy vehicles), MAP:MD-CHI05_Hint15 (Listening Outposts stop him sniping vehicles), ACADEMY:BuildAHero (the three heroes stay hidden from the enemy, and a player may have only one at once) and CONTROLBAR:ToolTipGLAUpgradeAPBullets (a quarter more damage).

sources.title: GLAInfantry.ini, unedited Zero Hour 1.04 game files, TheSuperHackers' GeneralsGamePatch repository on GitHub
sources.note: Kell's object, GLAInfantryJarmenKell: display name, one transport slot, one alive at a time, the rifle as primary weapon and the crew-kill rifle as a secondary that only its button fires, Human Armor, the vision and fog-clearing figures, the Barracks and Palace as prerequisites, price and build time, ranks, a crushable level with no squish module, the HERO and STEALTH_GARRISON kinds, health, his own locomotor, innate stealth that is forbidden while attacking, returns after a short delay and sends idle enemies at him when he is revealed, the AP Bullets bonus, and death animations with no blast. The Rebel's object in the same file wears Human Armor too.

sources.title: Weapon.ini, unedited Zero Hour 1.04 game files, TheSuperHackers' GeneralsGamePatch repository on GitHub
sources.note: GLAJarmenKellRifle: SNIPER damage, a reach a little over twice the Ranger's rifle, an effectively instant shot, no clip, the AP Bullets bonus, and no anti-air flag, so it cannot fire at aircraft. GLAJarmenKellVehiclePilotSniperRifle: KILL_PILOT damage at the same reach, one shot, then a clip reload of about half a minute. USAPathfinderSniperRifle, the Pathfinder's, reaches further than Kell's rifle.

uncertain.note: Roles step 1 reads the manual's Purpose entry, Scout and Base Infiltration. Both roles meet their requires (scout through the cloak passive's stealth-and-deception category), but neither has a target, so neither wins the bonus test and step 1 goes on; step 3 then gives marksman, because the main weapon is a sniper rifle that reaches long. The registry note reads every general's version as carrying the base-game Purpose entry, and all four Kell build buttons share one tooltip.

Scout and infiltrator both rank at roles.secondary step 1 (the Purpose entry), kept in the roles list's order. Two lower candidates are left out: anti-armour from the Sniper Attack button, which harms only vehicles (step 2), and anti-infantry from the rifle, which the tooltip calls strong against infantry (step 3). Infiltrator rests on Base Infiltration, on his hidden garrisoning and on the vehicle theft the snipe sets up; the roles tie-break keeps infiltrator for theft from inside, and Kell works from outside the vehicle, so that part of the fit is loose.

The wiki infobox and the 1.04 Weapon.ini both give a reload of about half a minute, the medium band. CNCNZ's GLA units page (https://cncnz.com/games/generals/gla-units/, a long-standing fan site, kind guide; read, not cited) lists the Sniper Attack with an instant cooldown. No official text gives a figure. The band follows the game data and the wiki. Being an uncited guide page, CNCNZ carries no code and does not count toward confidence, which counts only the cited pages; they all agree, so the entry stays high.

hijack-vehicle, as research/registry-notes/patterns.md folds a snipe that kills a vehicle's crew into it: the snipe removes the crew so that the vehicle can be taken, while the taking itself is the game-wide rule for empty vehicles. execute-target (its ranged-shot variant) was weighed, since the shot takes one kind of target out of the fight whatever its armour, but the vehicle is not destroyed and either side can claim it afterwards, which is hijack-vehicle's interaction.

Several details rest on pages read but not cited. EA's Zero Hour source release (official, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electronicarts/CnC_Generals_Zero_Hour/main/GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Body/ActiveBody.cpp): kill-pilot damage leaves a vehicle unhurt, unmanned, idle and on the neutral side, and a Combat Cycle is blown up if moving or scuttled once its rider is killed if parked. The same release's Source/GameLogic/Object/Object.cpp: riders are thrown out as the vehicle changes side, a sniped car bomb explodes, and an unmanned vehicle crushes nobody. Armor.ini of the unedited 1.04 files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Armor.ini): every vehicle armour set takes full kill-pilot damage, while the Sentry Drone, aircraft, building and soldier sets take none. The dozer trick, the forced exit of riders and the ban on sniping from a building are on the cited wiki page.

The stealth rules (hidden except while attacking, back after a short delay, idle enemies sent at him when revealed, hidden garrisoning) come from his 1.04 Object file and the registry's Generals stealth note. The Garrisoning page of the Command & Conquer Wiki (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Garrisoning, read, not cited) also says he and Pathfinders can garrison unseen, and that soldiers in a garrison are safe from their sniping. The Zero Hour manual scan (https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/cnc_gamepedia_en/images/b/b1/CNC_Generals_Zero_Hour_Manual_2015.pdf/revision/latest, read, not cited) says the Toxin and Demolition Generals, who field no other stealth, keep Kell's.

The soldier rule compares his set with the basic rifleman's: that the Ranger and Pathfinder wear the same Human Armor rests on AmericaInfantry.ini of the unedited 1.04 files (address under armament/0/summary, read, not cited); the Rebel's object in the cited GLAInfantry.ini wears it too. The class itself comes from the armour_map (step 1).

Infantry and structures. The wiki's prose calls the rifle useless against most targets that are not infantry, and its trivia names the Fire Base as the one building that takes sniper damage, the rest being blocked. Armor.ini of the unedited 1.04 files (read, not cited; address under abilities/0) agrees: every vehicle, aircraft and nearly every building set takes nothing from sniper damage, the Fire Base set takes it in full, and the Stinger Site set lets snipers hit the soldiers inside. Structures fall outside the sniper family's target list, which the validator records as atypical. The infobox's lore field calls the real rifle behind it anti-infantry; read as a label under can_target step 3 it would give the same list.

That each hit drops a basic rifleman is reasoned from game data: the rifle's damage, doubled by Human Armor's sniper value, is more than the Ranger's health in AmericaInfantry.ini of the unedited 1.04 files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/AmericaInfantry.ini, read, not cited) and the Rebel's in the cited GLAInfantry.ini. The wiki says only that his shots pick off infantry with ease.

That every GLA general fields him rests on uncited 1.04 files of the same repository: CommandSet.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/CommandSet.ini) puts a Kell build button in each general's Barracks, and the general's own objects in Object/ChemicalGeneral.ini, Object/DemoGeneral.ini and Object/StealthGeneral.ini need that general's Barracks and Palace, at the same price. The Zero Hour manual (address under abilities/1) also names him under the Toxin and Demolition Generals.

The Demolition General's version is described from uncited 1.04 files: Object/DemoGeneral.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/DemoGeneral.ini) gives his copy the timed and remote charges, which take several seconds to plant and reveal him, and, once the Demolitions upgrade is bought, a suicide button and death weapons; CommandSet.ini (address under tier) adds the matching buttons. The cited wiki page names the charges as Juhziz's only. Abilities have no notes field, so the difference is recorded here, beside the upgrade this field must name.

The wiki names only the Sentry Drone as an uncrewed counter; Armor.ini (read, not cited; address under abilities/0) shows that its armour set takes no kill-pilot damage. Whether every other drone resists the snipe is not covered by the sources read.

Partly reasoned: the Pathfinder's longer reach comes from the cited Weapon.ini and the double damage from his armour set's sniper value (wiki infobox); the wiki itself says only that a Combat Cycle shields him from counter-sniping Pathfinders and enemy Kells.

atypical.note: The rifle hurts one kind of building: the Fire Base takes sniper damage in full (wiki trivia; Armor.ini of the 1.04 files), while every other building is immune to it, so structures are listed although the sniper family leaves them out.
